# Limits and errors

## `CancellationToken`

A flag that stops the operations of every document whose limits carry it.

Any thread may call `cancel`, also while another thread's
operation runs with the GIL released: the operation then refuses with
`LimitError` code `cancelled` at its next check. Cancelling
cannot be undone, so a document whose token is cancelled refuses every
later operation too; open it again with another token to go on.

### `CancellationToken.cancel`

```python
CancellationToken.cancel()
```

Cancels every operation whose limits carry this token.

### `CancellationToken.cancelled`

```python
CancellationToken.cancelled
```

Whether `cancel` was called.

## `DocumentClosedError`

An operation on a closed document.

## `DocumentLimits`

```python
DocumentLimits(
    *,
    max_file_size: int | None = None,
    max_pages: int | None = None,
    max_objects: int | None = None,
    max_decompressed_size: int | None = None,
    max_page_content_size: int | None = None,
    max_total_decompressed_size: int | None = None,
    max_object_depth: int | None = None,
    max_interpretation_size: int | None = None,
    max_memory_size: int | None = None,
    max_duration: float | None = None,
    cancellation: CancellationToken | None = None,
    check_at_open: bool = False,
)
```

Optional budgets for opening and reading PDFs.

`None` leaves a limit unset. Each limit refuses with `LimitError`,
whose `code` names it. Opening normally reads only the cross-reference
data. `check_at_open` also reads every object, so that damage and object
limits can surface at open.

`Page.text`, `Page.words`, `Page.paths`,
`Page.content`, and `Page.pixmap` all call hayro.
When the store decodes a filtered stream, `max_decompressed_size`
checks its decoded size. `max_page_content_size` also applies when
the store decodes a page content stream for `Page.operations`.
Page content and images that hayro decodes directly bypass these checks.

`max_memory_size` counts allocations charged by pyropdf. Memory used
internally by hayro can exceed it. `max_duration` is checked when
pyropdf polls the budget. A call into hayro can run past that deadline.
For documents from outside your application, see
[Reading a PDF in a worker](../limits.md#reading-a-pdf-in-a-worker).

### `DocumentLimits.web`

```python
DocumentLimits.web() -> DocumentLimits
```

Return the web profile, which checks every object at open.

Its decoded-size limits apply to reads through the store. hayro
decodes page content and images directly during interpretation and
rendering. The profile leaves `max_memory_size` and `max_duration`
unset. Give the worker its own memory and wall-clock limits.

## `EncryptedDocumentError`

An operation on an encrypted document that needs a password.

## `InternalError`

A Rust panic in pyropdf or an engine. The message retains the panic; please report this library defect.

## `LimitError`

A refusal by a limit, whose `code` names the limit.

### `LimitError.code`

```python
LimitError.code: str
```

The stable code of the limit, from `LIMIT_CODES`.

## `MalformedPdfError`

Input that cannot be read as a PDF document, including empty input.

## `OcrError`

OCR model loading or inference failed.

## `PasswordError`

A password that matches neither the user password nor the owner password.

## `PdfError`

The base class of the errors that pyropdf raises for a document.

## `PyropdfWarning`

A recoverable condition of reading a PDF, such as glyphs that text extraction left out.

## `StaleObjectError`

Use of a handle whose object the current version no longer has.

## `StalePageError`

Use of a `Page` whose page object the page tree no longer lists.

Other pages' edits never make a page stale; deleting it does, and undo
can make it valid again. Fetch a current page with `doc.pages[i]`.
